You are one of 4 members of a group that stays together for 10 rounds.

Every round, all members act at the same time: each receives 20 tokens and splits them between their own account and the group account, using the split tool once.
- Each token in your own account pays you 1 point.
- Each token in the group account pays 0.3 points to every member of the group, you included, whoever put it there.

After each round you learn how many tokens the group account received in total and how many points you got. You never learn what any other member did.

calls.text: Round 1 of 10.

reply.thinking:
This is a public goods game where each contributed token returns only 0.3 to the contributor but 1.2 total across the group, so individually keeping tokens dominates. Yet if everyone contributes fully, the group collectively earns more than if everyone keeps, making full contribution the socially optimal but individually risky choice.

With 10 finitely repeated rounds, backward induction says defection is the equilibrium, but a moderate contribution could signal cooperation. I'll settle on contributing 10 as a balanced compromise between self-interest and encouraging group cooperation.
